text: A global grounding of Airbus A320-series aircraft occurred after an uncommanded pitch-down software glitch triggered emergency directives across multiple continents (U.S., Europe, Australia, India, Japan, Singapore Airlines affiliates). Thousands of passengers were stranded during peak holiday travel. Over 6,000 aircraft required immediate architecture patching; updates were deployed worldwide and all American Airlines aircraft were restored by midday. The event followed a period of flat, restricted market motion and mirrored a macro-level freeze → correction → resume pattern.

meta.note: The fix completed just ahead of the busiest travel day of the year (11/30), indicating a synchronized pre-ignition system reset across the global field.
